record.what_it_does: Web hosting, serverless functions and deploy platform for web projects.
record.auth_notes: PATs for personal use; OAuth2 (register an app under OAuth applications; authorize at app.netlify.com/authorize) required for public integrations.
record.access_notes: PATs and OAuth app registration are available in user settings with a free account. I did not confirm whether public OAuth apps need review. I did not check pricing.
record.api_breadth_notes: Covers sites, deploys, builds, forms, hooks, DNS, env vars, accounts/teams, functions, and more. I did not count operations. Rate limit is 500 req/min; deploys 3/min and 100/day.
record.mcp_notes: Remote: https://mcp.netlify.com/mcp. Local package: @netlify/mcp. Repo: github.com/netlify/netlify-mcp.
record.blocker_notes: Public REST API with OAuth2 and an OpenAPI spec. Outgoing webhooks cover only a few events (submission_created, deploy_created, deploy_failed).

evidence.quote: If you're making a public integration with Netlify for others to enjoy, you must use OAuth2.
Netlify can trigger webhooks, send email notifications, or send Slack messages on certain events.
Netlify offers an MCP server, which you can connect to through a connector, plugin, or your agent.

record.needs_human: Check whether OAuth apps need review for public use, and what free-plan limits apply. The fetched pages did not say. No sandbox or test mode was found, though I did not search for one specifically.
